title: Telemetry Signal Calibration and Operator Fatigue Retrospective — Q1 2026
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview
--------
This retrospective reviews a three-week campaign (2026-01-15 to 2026-02-05) where noisy telemetry, duplicated alert signals, and an off-nominal sampling configuration caused repeated oncall interruptions and elevated operator fatigue across the Platform Operators team. The doc summarizes the incident timeline, root causes, operator impact, mitigation steps, and concrete corrective actions that were adopted and rolled out in February 2026.

Background
----------
What happened: During a region-wide config rollout to increase sampling granularity for prefix-cache misses, a misapplied rewrite caused certain low-entropy telemetry events to surface as high-severity SLO alerts. Alerts were fired on: token-latency-99p, kv-prefix-cache-miss-rate, and runtime-op-rate-limit-errors due to correlated instrumentation amplification.

Why this matters: Frequent, high-noise alerts erode trust in dashboards, increase mean time to repair (MTTR) for genuine incidents, and materially increased operator cognitive load during an otherwise low-impact performance experiment.

Timeline (abridged)
------------------
1. 2026-01-15 09:00 — Sampling roll-out begins targeting regional cache frontends.
2. 2026-01-15 11:45 — First burst of kv-prefix-cache-miss-rate alerts; paging threshold exceeded.
3. 2026-01-15 12:30 — Operators acknowledge alerts; multiple duplicate tickets created from separate alert rules.
4. 2026-01-16 — Short-term mitigation: escalation rule adjusted to suppress duplicate signals (adhoc).
5. 2026-01-20 — Investigation identifies a telemetry enrichment step that duplicated event counts for sharded prefix caches when sampling_rate > 0.75.
6. 2026-01-25 — Permanent fix deployed to enrichment pipeline.
7. 2026-02-01 — Post-fix dashboard tuning and new alert gating rules rolled out.
8. 2026-02-05 — Formal retrospective and operator survey initiated.

Measured Impact
---------------
- Total pages during incident window: 142 (normal baseline: ~18/week).
- Average time-to-acknowledge (TTA): 7m 12s (baseline: 3m 20s).
- Average time-to-resolve (TTR): 1h 42m (baseline: 35m).
- Oncall burnout signal (anonymous survey): 62% reported "high" cognitive load; 28% considered stepping down from rotation.

Root causes
-----------
- Telemetry configuration: Sampling granularity changed without a coordinated cross-team validation plan. The enrichment job inadvertently multiplied counts for sharded cache keys.
- Alert design: Overlapping alert rules lacked de-duplication and grouping semantics. Independent rules paged the same operator for the same underlying event.
- Dashboard ergonomics: No single-pane view combined token-cost and kv-cache signals with request attribution (tenant ID, model-version), making triage slower.
- Runbook gaps: Oncall playbooks did not include a rapid dedupe mechanism or CLI snippet to silence noise across multiple alert sources.

Immediate mitigations taken
-------------------------
1. Rolled back the high-sampling variant for the enrichment pipeline (2026-01-16 03:00).
2. Added a temporary alert suppression tier for cached noisy signals for 48 hours while debugging.
3. Consolidated three overlapping PagerDuty escalation policies into a single grouped policy for cache-related SLI alerts.
4. Added a short CLI helper to silence grouped alerts:

   # Silence grouped cache alerts for 30m
   pd-silence --policy "cache-grouped" --duration 30m --author maya.patel@redwood.com

Technical root-cause analysis (summary)
-------------------------------------
- The enrichment job took sampled events and applied a join to per-shard metadata. Because sampling was applied upstream but the join operated pre-aggregation, it produced duplicate rows for multi-shard keys. The downstream metric emitter did event_count++ for each row, thus amplifying counts by shard cardinality.
- An innocuous configuration flag `preserve_shard_rows=true` had a default change during the roll-out PR; testing missed the scenario where sampling_rate was high.

Corrective actions (accepted and prioritized)
-------------------------------------------
A. Telemetry pipeline hardening (owner: eng-platform/telemetry; owner: Jun Park) — Complete by 2026-03-01
   - Add unit + integration tests that validate emitted cardinality against a golden sample (target tolerance +-2%).
   - Introduce a canary gate: sampling config changes must run on 1% production traffic for 24h with automated sanity checks.
   - Add a lint rule in cfg-repo that prevents `preserve_shard_rows=true` from being set without explicit justification and a reviewer tag.

B. Alert consolidation and dedupe (owner: eng-platform/observability; owner: Liam O'Connor) — Complete by 2026-02-20
   - Replace three cache-related rules with a single rule that exports a `cache_incident_id` label for grouping.
   - Implement contact-wise dedupe in PagerDuty: one page per incident_id per escalation window.
   - Reduce severity of kv-prefix-cache-miss-rate from P1->P2 when 95p latency < SLO.

C. Dashboard and triage UX improvements (owner: Platform Dashboards; owner: Sofia Ramirez) — Complete by 2026-02-28
   - New "Cache Triage" dashboard combining: token-latency-99p, kv-prefix-cache-miss-rate, and per-tenant request traces.
   - Add a top-level header for ongoing experiments and their rollout windows.

D. Runbook and oncall policy updates (owner: eng-sre; owner: Maya Patel) — Complete by 2026-02-15
   - Add dedupe CLI snippet (see Immediate mitigations).
   - Add explicit steps for validating sampling rollouts and a checklist for experiment owners.
   - Adjust rotation policy: limit consecutive oncall weeks to 2 during active experiment windows; require a secondary operator for the first 72 hours of any telemetry change.

Updated SLI/alert configuration (published values)
-------------------------------------------------
| metric                               | old threshold           | new threshold / gating                            | severity |
|--------------------------------------|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|----------|
| token-latency-99p (region)           | 200ms (alert @ 220ms)   | same, but gate by incident fingerprinting         | P1 -> P1 |
| kv-prefix-cache-miss-rate (global)   | 0.8% (alert)            | alert only if sustained for 5m and backed by error spikes | P1 -> P2 |
| runtime-op-rate-limit-errors         | 0.05%                  | require correlated latency or tenant error rate   | P1 -> P2 |

(Above table is a concise representation. Full prometheus rule files are in: git@infra:redwood/observability/alert-rules/tree/2026/sampling-safety)

Rollout plan for fixes
----------------------
1. Merge pipeline tests and lint rule (telemetry-team).
2. Run sampling canary for 24h on 1% traffic; automatic check must pass (metric cardinality within tolerance).
3. If canary passes, stage config to 10% traffic for 48h with operators on standby.
4. After 72h without anomalies, incrementally expand to 100% per normal change windows.

Owner matrix and dates
---------------------
- Jun Park (eng-platform/telemetry) — tests + canary gate — due 2026-03-01
- Liam O'Connor (eng-platform/observability) — alert dedupe changes — due 2026-02-20
- Sofia Ramirez (dashboards) — Cache Triage dashboard — due 2026-02-28
- Maya Patel (eng-sre) — runbook updates + rotation policy — due 2026-02-15

Acceptance criteria (how we will confirm closure)
------------------------------------------------
- Pages/week reduced to baseline ±10% for six consecutive weeks.
- Operator survey score "high cognitive load" reduced from 62% to <20% in next quarterly pulse.
- Canary cardinality checks integrated and in CI; PRs that change sampling require passing canary check.
- Dashboard has live links and owner; triage time (TTR) returns to baseline within 30 days of rollout.

Follow-ups (action items)
------------------------
- [ ] Run a 1-week simulated experiment with platform-operators as observers to validate dedupe behaviors (owner: Platform Operators).
- [ ] Add an incident tag to the status page for "telemetry calibration" experiments for increased visibility.
- [ ] Quarterly review of alert rules: maintain a short list of 10 high-noise candidates for potential suppression.

Appendix: diagnostic queries and CLI snippets
-------------------------------------------
1) Prometheus example: compare emitted cardinality by shard\\n   sum by (shard) (increase(prefix_cache_event_count[10m]))
2) Golden sample test (py)test snippet (example):
   assert abs(emitted_cardinality - expected_cardinality) < expected_cardinality * 0.02
3) PagerDuty dedupe example:
   pd-rule create --name "cache-incident-grouping" --label incident_id --dedupe true

Links and references
--------------------
- Incident ticket: INF-2026-3067
- Observability repo: git@infra:redwood/observability
- Runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/operator-safe-mode-and-manual-intervention-playbook-2026
- Dashboard template: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cache-triage-template

Conclusion
----------
This retrospective surfaced a recurring risk pattern: changing telemetry sampling and enrichment without small-scale canaries and cardinality tests produces noisy, trust-eroding alerts and operational overhead. The prioritized corrective actions focus on adding automated guards in the pipeline, consolidating alert logic with grouping/labels, improving triage UX, and reducing operator load through policy changes.

If you own any action item above, update the ticket INF-2026-3067 with progress and expected blockers.
